profile.name: Nathan Jerald
profile.role: IT Undergraduate Â· Full-Stack & Cloud-Native Developer
profile.summary: I'm Nathan, an Information Technology undergraduate at Thiagarajar College of Engineering who enjoys turning ideas into working software. My projects span full-stack applications, cloud-native security monitoring and blockchain-backed systems, with a growing interest in building memorable interactive experiences. NATHAN.EXE is where I bring that engineering curiosity together with the personal chapters that shaped me.
about: I like building things that people can use, not just prototypes that look impressive in screenshots. At TCE, I've explored full-stack web development, cloud and security tooling, and team-based hackathons. From an agricultural supply-chain platform to Kubernetes security monitoring, I enjoy moving between the user experience and the systems behind it.

Outside code, fitness has been a long-running part of my life: my journey moved from roughly 100 kg to 60 kg, and later to around 75 kg. I've also experienced studying abroad and beginning a new chapter at TCE in Madurai. This portfolio tells those stories as a small playable town, while keeping the actual work, resume and contact details one click away.

chapters.title: The Discipline
chapters.subtitle: Built one rep at a time
body: My fitness story doesn't fit into a before-and-after photo. I started around 100 kg, reached about 60 kg, and later moved toward a different kind of balance at roughly 75 kg. What stayed with me was the habit of showing up and making small improvements over time.
That same idea follows me into software: learn what you need, test what you've built, and keep improving it. The Iron Yard is where this save file reminds me that progress is rarely a straight line.

chapters.title: The First Chapter
chapters.subtitle: Tomsk State University
body: My university journey began at Tomsk State University in Russia. I spent two semesters studying there, getting to know a different academic environment and a different place.
Winter Campus is a snapshot of that part of my life. Not every chapter has to explain what came next; some deserve a space of their own.

chapters.title: The Next Chapter
chapters.subtitle: Thiagarajar College of Engineering, Madurai
body: At Thiagarajar College of Engineering in Madurai, I continued my B.Tech in Information Technology. TCE became the place where coursework met real projects: hackathon builds, technical events, team collaboration, and the first versions of ideas that became much bigger.
The wins were exciting, but so were the ordinary parts of learning: debugging, presenting, and figuring out how to ship something with a team.
highlights: IT Association office bearer Â· E-Cell

chapters.title: The Builder
chapters.subtitle: Ideas in, projects out
body: The Garage is where prototypes become something you can click, test and question. There are projects here about agriculture, cloud security, web systems and new ways to tell a story, each with the problem, the build and what it taught me.

chapters.title: The Toolbox
chapters.subtitle: What I've learned
body: No one builds alone, and no one knows every tool. Signal Tower is a map of the languages, systems and teams I've worked with, from web development and cloud security to project competitions and testing.

chapters.title: The Next Mission
chapters.subtitle: Where this save file goes next
body: This save file isn't finished. I want to keep building dependable software, learning from good teams, and making ideas that are useful as well as memorable.
If one of these projects sparks a conversation, I'd love to hear from you. The game ends here, but the next collaboration could start with a message.

chapters.title: The Beginning
chapters.subtitle: St. Montfort Higher Secondary School, Trichy
body: Before the projects, the competitions, and the unexpected journeys, there was Montfort. Classrooms, familiar faces, and the ordinary days that quietly became the beginning of everything.

projects.title: Aratro: Agricultural Supply Chain Platform
projects.pitch: Tracing agricultural supply chains from farmers to distribution, with blockchain-backed workflows.
projects.description: Agricultural supply flows need clear visibility across farmers, warehouses and ration shops. In a team, I developed warehouse and inventory workflows and integrated Python-backed processes with Solidity smart contracts on an Ethereum/Ganache setup, covering MSP information, quality checks and inventory tracking. Won 1st place at Hack Odyssey 2K25, a 24-hour hackathon.
architecture: Farmer â†’ Warehouse â†’ Ration shop supply flow
Python-backed workflows: warehouse, inventory, quality checks, MSP information
Solidity smart contracts on a local Ethereum chain (Ganache) record each step
projects.contribution: Developed the warehouse and inventory workflows and integrated the Python-backed processes with the Solidity smart contracts (MSP information, quality checks and inventory tracking).

projects.title: Microservices Security Logging Framework
projects.pitch: Making Kubernetes activity easier to observe through runtime security alerts and dashboards.
projects.description: Security events from containers and clusters are hard to review when they live in disconnected logs. During the HPE Career Preview Program, I contributed to a Kubernetes-based monitoring pipeline using Falco detection and Grafana dashboards, combining runtime activity with cluster and audit-event visibility.
projects.contribution: Contributed to the Kubernetes-based monitoring pipeline: Falco runtime detection feeding Grafana dashboards, with cluster and audit-event visibility.

projects.title: TCE Event Scheduler
projects.pitch: Scheduling department events with practical admin and database workflows.
projects.description: Built during a six-hour hackathon: a Flask and SQL event scheduler with an HTML/CSS frontend, focused on user navigation and database connectivity. Runner-up at HackFest 2025.

projects.title: CauverySite: Real Estate Management Platform
projects.pitch: A role-aware property management platform for sales teams and administrators.
projects.description: Property sales teams need a structured way to manage staff and see business operations. I built an application with Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS featuring role-specific dashboards, an employee hierarchy, profiles and sales overview modules.
projects.contribution: Built the application: role-specific dashboards, the employee hierarchy, profiles and the sales overview modules.

projects.title: NATHAN.EXE: Play My Save File
projects.pitch: An interactive game portfolio built around the chapters of my life.
projects.description: A compact 2.5D retro town with a playable character, fast travel on the Memory Line, collectible stories, interactive project exhibits and a recruiter-friendly quick view. In progress.

projects.title: Hospital Management System
projects.pitch: My first UI project: a desktop app for managing hospital patient records, built in school.
projects.description: Built in Class XII at St. Montfort as my first project with a real user interface. A Python desktop app made with Tkinter that lets hospital staff log in, add and search patient records, and keep the data saved between sessions in binary files. It was where I first learned to think about screens, buttons and how someone actually uses software.
architecture: Tkinter windows: login, patient records, search
Python logic for adding, finding and updating records
Records stored on disk in binary files so data persists between runs
Custom icons and background images for the interface
projects.contribution: Designed and built the whole app on my own, from the login screen and icons to the record storage.

experience.summary: Contributed to a team-built Kubernetes security logging and monitoring project, integrating Falco event detection and Grafana dashboards for better cluster visibility.
Tested web and mobile functionality, documented defects, verified fixes and gave usability feedback, using tools including Reflect and BugBug.io.
Supported volunteer coordination for technical and cultural events.
Helped organise events and activities, including flagship events with 800+ participants, and hosted "The Good, The Bad & The Ugly", a survival-themed entrepreneurship event.

npcs.name: Thianesh
lines: Back for another session? The Iron Yard keeps score in clean reps, not words.
topics: Let's hit a heavy set on the rack! :: Three clean reps! Tight groove, chest up, push through the floor! [action:gym-lift]
How would you describe Nathan's fitness journey? :: Roughly 100 kg down to 60, then built back up to a solid 75 kg. One habit: showing up.
What is the secret to recovery? :: Quality sleep, adequate protein, and never underestimating post-workout nutrition.

npcs.name: Guru
lines: Minus twenty outside, but Tomsk State University keeps the code hot!
topics: Let's take the scooty for a spin! :: Keys are in the ignition! Watch the tight corners and enjoy the ride. [action:scooter-ride]
Remember our Tomsk semester? :: Walking to class with frozen eyelashes! Russian history lectures were legendary.
How is that compiler bug coming along? :: Found it at three in the morning! Classic missing semicolon in the async handler.

npcs.name: Shabeer
lines: Some of us have been around since the very first chapter, Nathan.
topics: Can we look through the memory album? :: Opening the archive now. Every chapter has an unforgettable memory. [action:open-album]
Remember our classroom days at Montfort? :: Trading lunch boxes, last minute exam prep, and laughing until our stomachs hurt. Golden times.
Read any inspiring books recently? :: Finished a great piece on discipline and daily habits. Small consistent actions compound massively.

npcs.name: Anu
lines: You found TCE! There is always an event or a hackathon happening here.
topics: Remember that hackathon crunch night at TCE? :: Coding all night, cheering when the demo finally ran, and walking out to sunrise breakfast! Unforgettable.
What makes the TCE chapter special? :: Long walks across campus, project marathons, and friends who always have your back.
You always kept the team calm under pressure. :: Someone had to! You were ready to rewrite the entire database at 4 AM.

npcs.name: Akshai
lines: Welcome to the Garage! Ideas come in, clean builds ship out.
topics: How does the Aratro build test out? :: Passed all stress tests! Hack Odyssey first place was well earned. [action:project-aratro]
What hardware upgrade makes the biggest difference? :: Fast NVMe storage and dual-channel memory. Never let compilation wait on disk I/O.
The garage crew motto still stands? :: 'Ship it now, optimize it later!' Classic engineering reality.

npcs.name: Naveen
lines: Mind the cables, Nathan! Something is always compiling, but chai comes first.
topics: Who is winning on the carrom board today? :: My center striker has been deadly! White coins are mine, and loser buys snacks.
What is your favorite part of this whole crew? :: How everyone lifts each other up. Whether launching apps or playing games, nobody walks alone.
Chai break first, code second. :: Words of true wisdom. A five-minute chai break has solved more bugs than staring at a screen.

npcs.name: Shabesh
lines: Filming the college campus today. Capturing the moments while they are happening.
topics: If Nathan's journey were a film, what genre? :: A coming-of-age comeback story. Big challenges, loyalty, and a soundtrack that hits just right.
What makes a shot truly memorable? :: Not the camera body. It is the genuine emotion captured in an unscripted moment.
Hey, this whole town is one of your biggest productions. :: Still expanding, district by district. Every building represents a real milestone.

npcs.name: Harris
lines: Pre-flight checks complete, captain! Ready for Tahiti?
topics: Wheels up, Harris! Fly to Tahiti. :: Strap in, Nathan. Clearing runway one-niner for takeoff to Tahiti! [action:fly-tahiti]
Let's roll film at the outdoor cinema! :: Projector light is rolling! Marvel movie marathon is on screen. [action:pop_cinema]
Who is your all-time favorite Avenger? :: Iron Man, without question. Genius, builder, and he pilots his own high-speed thrusters!

npcs.name: Tyler Durden
lines: Ever wondered how much of you is actually yours?
topics: What defines a person? :: Not the stuff on the shelf, that's for sure. // Take away the furniture and the job title and see what's still standing. That's the part worth working on.
Is change always a good thing? :: No. Change is just pressure. // What matters is whether you chose it, or whether it happened while you weren't looking.
What would you tell Nathan? :: Build things you actually believe in. // Not for the trophy shelf. For the version of you that's still there after the applause.
Can I hit the bag? :: Go on. One clean hit. Then let it go. [action:pop_boxing]

npcs.name: Arthur Morgan
lines: Long road, partner. What brings you out here?
topics: What makes a good life? :: Folks you'd ride back for. // A fire at night, honest work, and somebody who'd notice if you didn't come home.
Do our choices define us? :: Every one of 'em leaves a track. // You can't always pick the trail you're on. You can pick how you walk it.
What do you think about Nathan's journey? :: Took a few turns most wouldn't. // Way I see it, the detours taught him more than the straight roads ever could.

npcs.name: Moon Knight
npcs.role: Knight of the moon Â· Moonlit court
lines: Funny how different the world looks under another light.
topics: Can someone have different sides? :: Everyone does. Most people just never introduce them to each other. // The trick is getting them to work together instead of taking turns.
What makes us who we are? :: The stories we keep telling ourselves. // And the nerve to rewrite one when it stops being true.
What do you see in Nathan? :: Someone who has already been a few different people. // Athlete, student abroad, builder. Same person underneath, still finding out what comes next.
Is there anything hidden here? :: Look closely at the pool. Some things only show themselves when you pay attention. [action:pop_moon]

npcs.name: Spider-Man
lines: Hey! Nice place you've built here. Mind the rooftops.
topics: How do you handle responsibility? :: Badly, at first! // Then you learn you can't carry everything at once. You pick what matters, and you show up for it every day.
What happens when things go wrong? :: They go wrong. A lot. // You dust off, laugh about it later, and swing back in. Nobody gets it right on the first try.
Got any advice for Nathan? :: Don't forget the people who helped you up. // And maybe sleep between hackathons. Just a thought.
Want to try the rooftop run? :: Three red rings, fifteen seconds. Run through all of them. Go! [action:pop_web]

npcs.name: Daredevil
lines: You can learn a lot when you pay attention.
topics: What does strength really mean? :: Getting up quietly, every time, with nobody watching. // Most real strength never makes a sound.
How do you keep going? :: One more round. Then one more. // You don't need to see the whole road. You just need to hear the next step.
What would you tell Nathan? :: Listen more than you speak, and you'll hear what the problem really is. // Works for code, too.
Can you show me how you listen? :: Close your eyes. Hear that? [action:pop_rooftop_red] // Every sound comes back a little different. That's the city talking.

npcs.name: Richard Hendricks
npcs.role: Founder, Pied Piper Â· Startup desk
lines: So... technically it works. Just don't refresh it.
topics: What's the hardest part of coding? :: Naming things. Then explaining to everyone why you named them that. // Also the bug that only shows up during the demo.
Is building a startup worth it? :: Statistically? Probably not. // Personally? You learn more in six months than in six comfortable years. Also there are snacks.

What do you think about Nathan's projects? :: Supply chains on a blockchain, security dashboards, a scheduler built in six hours... // He ships things. Do you know how rare that is? My pitch deck is older than most of his repos.
Help me debug this build? :: Okay, watch the screen. Compiling... [action:pop_startup] // Red. Classic. One missing bracket later... // Green! Don't touch anything.

npcs.name: Logeshwaran
lines: Soldering some sensor pins. Hardware never lies, Nathan.
topics: Show me the security logging pipeline. :: Immutable logging stream across all microservices. Every audit event accounted for. [action:project-microservices]
What electronics project are you tinkering with? :: A decentralized sensor node network. Ultra low power consumption on solar.
Hardware or software? :: Hardware gives software physical hands. The real magic happens when they talk.

npcs.name: Piranav
npcs.role: Working on his laptop Â· TCE
lines: Just finishing up this schedule module. Deadlines keep the mind sharp!
topics: How did the TCE Event Scheduler turn out? :: Runner-up at HackFest 2025! Clean calendar algorithms and zero registration collisions. [action:project-scheduler]
How do you stay on top of heavy project workloads? :: Time blocking, automated testing, and clear milestones. Never let ambiguity slow you down.
Taking breaks is part of the system. :: Absolutely. Step away, reset your focus, then execute.

npcs.name: Prince
lines: Freezing out here in Tomsk, but cold weather builds mental stamina!
topics: Crack any interesting security flags lately? :: Pwned a binary exploitation box yesterday. Buffer overflow straight into root shell. Pure dopamine.
Defense in depth, right? :: Always. Bound your memory, sanitize inputs, and never trust unauthenticated packets.
What are you playing on your phone? :: High-reflex mobile games until my fingers freeze!
